cards.text: Chronicles has been rolling out family lines like dough with no end, and now it's the clans of Judah, one of Jacob's sons: Perez, Hezron, Hur, Ashhur the father of Tekoa with his two wives, and a sister named Hazzelelponi. HAZZELELPONI. Friend, I tried saying that out loud and my mustache tied itself in a knot.
Then, in the middle of all these names, the record slows down for one man: Jabez, more honorable than his brothers. And after Hazzelelponi, a name I can actually say? I already LIKE him.

cards.question: Jabez's mother is the one who named him. What reason does she give for the name Jabez?

answers.text: He was born in a strange land
He was born during a famine

cards.question: Jabez, the man named for his mother's pain, calls out with a big request. Who does he call out to?
In his prayer, Jabez asks God to bless him and enlarge his territory.
Jabez asks God's hand to be with him and keep him from harm, so that he will be free from ___.
God turns down the request of Jabez.

cards.text: Then the record goes back to Judah's clans, where Mered's wife is Bithiah, Pharaoh's daughter, and whole clans are known as craftsmen, linen workers and potters. Families known for what they MADE, while my one skill for years in that junk drawer was collecting DUST.

Next comes the line of Simeon, Judah's brother, living in towns like Beersheba and Ziklag: Shimei has sixteen sons and six daughters, but his brothers don't have many children, so the clan never gets as numerous as Judah's. Twenty-two children, friend, and I raised six little cookie cutters and STILL needed a nap.
The Simeonite clan leaders named in the record see their families increase greatly. That's the kind of growth where the family group chat gets so big NOBODY knows who half the people in it are.

cards.question: With their families growing, the Simeonites journey to the entrance of Gedor, east of the valley. They're searching for ___ for their flocks.
At Gedor, the Simeonites find land that's crowded and full of trouble.
The record says someone had lived at Gedor before the Simeonites showed up. Who was it?

cards.text: The men named in that list come in the days of Hezekiah, king of Judah, and attack the Hamites in their dwellings, and the Meunites who were there too. Friend, the record doesn't soften it one bit: they devote them to destruction.

cards.question: After the attack, the Simeonites settle in that land at Gedor. What reason does the record give?

answers.text: There was pasture for their flocks
The king had ordered them to stay
The cities there had strong walls

cards.text: And that's not the end of it. Five hundred Simeonites head out, led by Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi.

cards.question: Where do the five hundred Simeonites go?
At Mount Seir, the five hundred Simeonites strike down the remnant of the ___ who had escaped.
After the battle, the Simeonites stay at Mount Seir, and the record says they have lived there to this day.

findings.problem: Jabez's story in verses 9–10 is a short story embedded in the genealogy, but cards 3–7 give it five choice cards. It can be a standout detail in the summary of that long stretch, but it cannot receive choice cards.

rule.text: A short story inside the stretch, like Nimrod in the list of nations (Genesis 10:8–12), is part of the stretch: it can be the standout detail on that card, but it gets no choice cards.

findings.problem: Most choices are not informed guesses. The earlier cards give no way to reason out the mother's stated reason (card 3), the content or outcome of the prayer (cards 5 and 7), the land's condition or former inhabitants (cards 12–13), or the destination, enemy and final settlement (cards 17–19). This goes beyond a few discovery questions among mostly informed choices.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The description of Judah as one of Jacob's sons is a fact from outside 1 Chronicles 4:1–8, but no reference supporting that relationship is given.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Calling Simeon Judah's brother adds a relationship not stated in 1 Chronicles 4:24–37, and the card gives no reference for that outside fact.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.
